purpose: Version-gates the legacy pre-6.9 template_redirect output-buffer and script-defer fallback hook registrations in includes/class-main.php and includes/class-cache.php so the modern WP 6.9 template-enhancement buffer hooks are only used on 6.9+ core and the legacy paths are never registered there, preventing double buffer processing.
riskRationale: The code change itself is small, conservative, and provably behavior-preserving on supported WP 6.2-6.8, with no new core APIs or security surface. However, the commit bundles ~4,739 dev-only vendor files (~35MB / ~525K lines: PHPUnit, PHPCS, WPCS, Mockery, Patchwork, Brain Monkey, php-parser, sebastian/*, etc.) into the tracked vendor/ tree in direct violation of AGENTS.md's 'composer release' convention, and .distignore does not exclude most of them, so any packaging path that skips the composer step would ship test tooling in the production plugin ZIP.
breakingChanges: Tracked vendor/ inflated from 236 to ~4,967 files by committing dev-only test tooling (PHPUnit, Mockery, Patchwork, Brain Monkey, WPCS, php-parser, sebastian/*, etc.) that is not excluded by .distignore and would ship in the plugin artifact if packaging skips 'composer install --no-dev'

text: The version-gating logic is well-scoped and directionally correct: the belt-and-suspenders function_exists() && version_compare gates guarantee the legacy template_redirect buffer path is never registered on stable WP 6.9+ while preserving 6.2-6.8 behavior exactly, with clear removal TODOs. Two problems block merge: (1) ~4,739 dev-only vendor files are committed into the tracked vendor/ directory against AGENTS.md, and (2) the defer gate at class-main.php:343 is dead code backed by a factually wrong comment (wp_script_add_data exists since WP 4.2; only its 'strategy' key is honored from 6.3).

reasoning: The buffer gating is sound, but the commit must be cleaned before merge: strip dev-only dependencies via 'composer release' so vendor/ contains only production packages, and correct or remove the dead defer gate and its misleading comment (the true threshold is WP 6.3, where the native defer 'strategy' is honored). Minor follow-ups: make the 6.9 version gate pre-release-safe and drop the now-misleading _doing_it_wrong notice.

message: The belt-and-suspenders gate (function_exists( 'wp_should_output_buffer_template_for_enhancement' ) && $is_wp69_plus) correctly guarantees the modern wp_template_enhancement_output_buffer / wp_finalized_template_enhancement_output_buffer hooks are never registered on non-6.9 core and the legacy template_redirect buffer is never registered on 6.9+, eliminating any double-buffer/double-processing risk while preserving 6.2-6.8 behavior exactly.

The delay-JS branch is correctly left un-gated: add_defer_attribute genuinely performs the wppo-src/type rewriting for delay JS on all versions, so that path must remain registered regardless of WP version.

Keeping start_output_buffer() intact for WP < 6.9 with an updated deprecation message and explicit 'TODO: remove when minimum supported WP is raised to 6.9' markers is good maintenance hygiene and aligns with the repo's version-gated backward-compat conventions.
Clear TODO comments documenting when the legacy paths can be removed make the version-gated code self-documenting and easy to clean up later.

The commit adds ~4,739 files (~35MB, ~525K lines) of dev-only Composer packages to the tracked vendor/ tree: phpunit, mockery, hamcrest, brain/monkey, antecedent/patchwork, nikic/php-parser, all sebastian/*, phar-io/*, theseer/tokenizer, myclabs/deep-copy, squizlabs/php_codesniffer, wp-coding-standards/wpcs, phpcompatibility, staabm, etc. AGENTS.md explicitly requires running 'composer release' (composer install --no-dev) and committing only the production vendor (voku/html-min, matthiasmullie/minify, woocommerce/action-scheduler). The release workflow strips dev deps before packaging, but .distignore only excludes a subset (squizlabs, wp-coding-standards, phpcsstandards, dealerdirect, bin), so vendor/phpunit, vendor/sebastian, vendor/mockery, vendor/brain, vendor/antecedent, etc. would ship in the plugin ZIP if packaging ever skips the composer step. The PR description acknowledges this as a 'verification side-effect' yet commits it anyway.
suggestion: Before merging, run 'composer release' so vendor/ contains only the production dependencies, then commit the slimmed vendor/ tree; as belt-and-suspenders, add the remaining dev directories to .distignore so test tooling can never leak into a release artifact.
suggestionCode: composer release && git add vendor/ && git commit -m "fix: strip dev dependencies from vendor directory"

message: The new '&& ! $is_wp68_plus' clause is dead code and the accompanying comment ('WP 6.8+ always provides wp_script_add_data') is factually wrong. wp_script_add_data() has existed in core since WP 4.2, so '! function_exists( 'wp_script_add_data' )' is always false on every supported version (6.2+) and this defer fallback was never registered for deferJS before or after this PR. The 'strategy' key (defer/async) is only honored by core since WP 6.3, so the correct threshold is 6.3, not 6.8; on 6.2 the native strategy is silently ignored (pre-existing, not a fatal). The PR's stated goal of version-correcting the defer path is therefore not achieved, and the comment will mislead future maintainers.
suggestion: Simplify the branch to keep only the delay-JS registration path (the filter only rewrites tags for delay JS) and correct the comment to reference WP 6.3, where the defer 'strategy' key is actually honored; or if a hard gate is desired, use $is_wp63_plus instead of $is_wp68_plus.

message: version_compare( get_bloginfo( 'version' ), '6.9', '>=' ) returns false for pre-release/dev strings such as '6.9-beta1' or '6.9-RC1' (beta < stable in PHP version_compare), even though those exact builds ship wp_should_output_buffer_template_for_enhancement(). During the 6.9 beta/RC window the plugin would therefore select the legacy template_redirect path on core that already buffers via the enhancement hooks — the opposite of the PR's intent, and capable of re-introducing the double-buffer scenario. 6.9 is now stable and 7.x compares fine, so this is latent, but it will recur each major cycle.
suggestion: Gate the modern path primarily on function_exists() (which cannot exist on < 6.9 core) and treat the version check as a conservative secondary, or make the comparison pre-release-inclusive (e.g. version_compare( $version, '6.9-rc0', '>=' )) and document the quirk with a comment.

message: get_bloginfo( 'version' ) is invoked twice (lines 338-339) on every request in setup_hooks() — front-end, admin, REST, cron — even when none of the gated features are enabled, and it is filterable, so a theme/plugin bloginfo filter could skew both gates.
suggestion: Resolve the version once into a local variable (or use the unfiltered $wp_version global) and derive both booleans from it.

message: After this PR, start_output_buffer() is only registered on WP < 6.9, yet it still unconditionally triggers _doing_it_wrong() when WP_DEBUG && is_admin() on those exact versions — logging a false deprecation on every admin page load for the majority of installs. The reworded message ('deprecated on WP 6.9+') can never fire on a version where it is accurate, making it misleading dead weight.
suggestion: Remove the _doing_it_wrong() block entirely (the version gate already enforces the deprecation structurally) and keep only the TODO comment, or rescope the notice to fire only on 6.9+ via a direct-call guard.
